# Tran Quoc Dat

## SAP Experience

Tran Quoc Dat has hands-on SAP technical experience from university capstone work and on-the-job training at FPT Software.

- FPT Software: OJT Trainee, January 2025 to April 2025
- SAP focus: ABAP development, RAP-based service design, Fiori/UI5 user interfaces, OData integration, S/4HANA application behavior, enterprise documentation, and delivery reporting
- Notable SAP project: Custom Notification Center, a centralized notification experience inside SAP S/4HANA

## Selected Projects

- [Custom Notification Center](https://tranquocdat.com/projects/custom-notification-center): SAP capstone graduation project. Built a centralized notification center inside SAP S/4HANA with bell badge, dropdown notification list, read/unread controls, archive/delete actions, subscription settings, ABAP APIs, RAP/OData services, Fiori/UI5 UI, and near real-time delivery using WebSocket and AMC/APC. Role: Team Leader for a 4-member team.
- [Hengout](https://tranquocdat.com/projects/hengout): Startup product for Gen Z location discovery. Built personalized venue recommendations, group consensus suggestions, event-driven updates with Kafka, Redis caching, Apple In-App Purchase integration, Grafana monitoring, CI/CD, VPS deployment, and App Store delivery. Role: Tech Lead. Result: won a 50 million VND scholarship from FPT University and shipped to the App Store.
- [Koi Vet. Center](https://tranquocdat.com/projects/koi-vet-center): University course project for veterinary service workflows. Focused on full-stack application development and database-backed business features.
- [Uni. Event Manager](https://tranquocdat.com/projects/uni-event-manager): University course project for event management workflows. Focused on backend design, frontend integration, and practical team delivery.
- [AI Quick Note](https://tranquocdat.com/projects/ai-quick-note): University course project exploring AI-assisted note workflows and practical application design.
- [Other repositories](https://github.com/tqdat410?tab=repositories): Smaller experiments, utilities, and public source code.
